newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares up at noon on better sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares up at noon on better sentiment.

text.p: Shanghai's foreign currency B shares ended Friday morning higher on improved sentiment, but profit taking toward the morning close trimmed earlier gains, brokers said.
Sentiment was helped by gains in B shares in the previous two days, but investors remained cautious, they said.
The B index closed the morning up 0.592 points or 0.79 percent to 75.433 points on volume of 3.916 million shares worth $2.378 million.
"It was a technical rebound, so sentiment has improved," said a broker at a foreign securities firm in Shanghai, referring to the gains of the past two days.
But many investors were hesitant to buy as they waited to see if the government would make any further moves to stabilise the markets after a crackdown which began in May, brokers said.
Investors were also looking towards the reporting of 1997 interim results later this month and in August to provide fresh incentives to buy, they said.
The fining and one day suspension of Shenzhen-listed Foshan Lighting and Electrical Co Ltd on Friday for making illegal loans had little effect on the Shanghai market, brokers said.
"Foshan is relatively small and it wasn't a favourite," said an analyst at a European securities firm in Shanghai.
Of 45 Shanghai-listed B shares, 36 traded with 20 up, eight down and eight flat.
Shanghai Industrial Sewing Machinery Co was the sharpest B share gainer on speculative buying, rising $0.010 or 8.93 percent to $0.122.
Shanghai's domestic currency A share index also rose on improved sentiment, helped by recent positive newspaper reports about the stock market, brokers said.
The A index gained 9.172 points or 0.78 percent to 1,179.161 points on volume of 146.892 million shares worth 1.778 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index rose 13.006 points or 0.35 percent to 3,705.084 points.
The A and B share indices could move higher on Friday afternoon as retail investors were still looking to buy shares, brokers said.
